paper.title: Benchmark Everything Everywhere All at Once
paper.abstract: Benchmarks are fundamental for evaluating and advancing LLMs and MLLMs by providing standardized and explicit measures of performance. However, their construction is labor-intensive and hard to reuse, raising concerns about sustainability and scalability. Moreover, existing benchmarks often quickly reach performance saturation after their release, resulting in insufficient discrimination among state-of-the-art models. To address these challenges, we introduce Benchmark Agent, a fully autonomous

summary.core_problem: 论文要解决的是 benchmark 构建过程过度依赖人工、难复用、迭代慢，同时现有 benchmark 很快饱和，难以区分新模型能力差异的问题。它提出用一个自动化 agent 系统，把用户的抽象评测需求转成可运行、可刷新、可定制的 benchmark。
summary.importance: 这篇论文的核心贡献是评测基础设施，不是预训练方法。它对基座研究的启发在于，模型迭代速度已经超过很多静态 benchmark 的生命周期，评测资产需要从一次性人工构建转向可持续生成和质量控制。对 pretrain 研究员来说，它更适合作为评测管线和数据治理的参考：如何把能力维度拆成子任务，如何做样本生成、标注、过滤和一致性检查，如何控制 LLM-as-a-judge 带来的偏差。它不会直接告诉你如何训练更好的模型，但能帮助设计更贴近目标能力的评测闭环。
summary.technical_approach: Benchmark Agent 采用 Planner 和 Executor 两级结构。Planner 是高层决策模块，负责把用户需求解析成子任务集合、数据配置和 benchmark 转换方案，并检查每个子任务是否有可行的数据 grounding。Executor 是执行模块，按 Planner 的规格调用工具完成数据生成、标注、格式化和质量控制，最后产出可运行 benchmark。这个设计的取舍比较清楚：如果只用单个 LLM agent 端到端生成 benchmark，长链路任务容易失控，也难以对数据条件和执行约束做一致校验；Planner/Executor 拆分后，高层任务设计和底层数据处理可以分别约束。论文强调三个特性：面向用户需求的定制化、低人工成本下的质量控制、面向新模型和新领域的持续刷新。
summary.experiments: 论文实现 Benchmark Agent 并生成 15 个代表性 benchmark。引言中用 Qwen 和 Qwen-VL 系列的历史结果说明 benchmark 饱和现象：很多分数在短时间内超过 80%，剩余区分空间有限。评测部分包括人工评估、LLM-as-a-judge 评估、一致性检查、时间和成本分析，以及组件消融。根据给出的内容，作者声称生成 benchmark 在可靠性、区分度、效率和成本上都可接受；但当前材料没有列出具体人工一致率、成本数值、构建耗时或各消融项下降幅度。阅读时需要重点核对这些数字，否则很难判断系统是否真的适合高风险模型评测。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议 20 到 30 分钟。先看系统流程图和 Planner/Executor 的接口定义，确认它如何从一句自然语言评测需求落到子任务、数据源和评价指标。然后看质量控制部分，尤其是样本过滤、标注校验、一致性检查和 LLM judge 的使用方式。实验部分不必细读所有生成 benchmark 的案例，优先看人类评估和一致性结果，再看成本与构建时间。若用于内部评测建设，需要额外关注两点：生成数据是否会引入模型偏好，自动刷新是否会破坏不同模型版本之间的可比性。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses the cost and fragility of benchmark construction. Existing benchmarks are usually built by human-heavy, benchmark-specific pipelines, and many saturate quickly as model capabilities improve. Benchmark Agent aims to turn a high-level evaluation request into an executable, customizable, and refreshable benchmark with much less manual work.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is mainly evaluation infrastructure rather than a modeling or pretraining method. Its relevance to foundation-model research lies in evaluation lifecycle management. As model iteration accelerates, static benchmarks can lose discriminative power shortly after release. A reusable benchmark-building pipeline may help pretraining teams define finer-grained capabilities, generate targeted test sets, and maintain evaluation freshness. The key caution is quality control: automatically generated benchmarks must be checked for judge bias, annotation errors, data leakage, and comparability across model versions.
summary_en.technical_approach: Benchmark Agent uses a two-component design. The Benchmark Planner maps user requirements into concrete benchmark specifications, including subtask decomposition, data configuration, and transformation plans. It also checks whether each subtask can be grounded in available data. The Benchmark Executor then turns the plan into a runnable benchmark by using tools for sample generation, annotation, formatting, and quality control. This split is sensible for a long-horizon task: a single end-to-end agent would have to handle high-level task design, data constraints, execution details, and validation in one loop. Separating planning from execution makes the pipeline easier to constrain and audit.
summary_en.experiments: The system is used to produce 15 representative benchmarks. The introduction motivates the need with an analysis of Qwen and Qwen-VL benchmark results, where many scores exceed 80% within a short time, reducing headroom for discrimination. The evaluation covers human assessment, LLM-as-a-judge assessment, consistency checks for sample discriminativeness, time and cost efficiency, and ablations of system components. The provided text does not include exact agreement rates, construction costs, runtime numbers, or ablation deltas, so the strength of the empirical claim depends on the missing tables and appendices.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in 20 to 30 minutes. Focus on the system diagram and the Planner/Executor interface: how a natural-language evaluation need becomes subtasks, data sources, sample formats, and scoring rules. Then read the quality-control pipeline, especially filtering, annotation verification, consistency checks, and the use of LLM judges. In the experiments, prioritize human validation, discriminative-power tests, and cost/runtime analysis. If adapting the idea for internal model evaluation, pay special attention to two risks: generated benchmarks may inherit model-specific biases, and frequent benchmark refreshes may reduce comparability across model releases.

recommendation.zh: 核心idea有意思——用agent自动造benchmark解决评测饱和问题，但这类方法的数据质量和污染检测存疑，看摘要+实验设计即可。
recommendation.en: Interesting idea (agent-generated benchmarks to fight saturation), but data quality and contamination detection are open questions; read abstract + experimental design only.

paper.title: Goedel-Architect: Streamlining Formal Theorem Proving with Blueprint Generation and Refinement
paper.abstract: We introduce Goedel-Architect, an agentic framework for formal theorem proving in Lean 4 centered on blueprint generation and refinement. A blueprint is a dependency graph of definitions and lemmas that builds up to the main theorem. First, Goedel-Architect generates a blueprint of formally stated definitions and lemmas, along with declared dependencies. This blueprint is optionally guided by a natural language proof. Then, a tool-equipped Lean prover component closes each open lemma node in par

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的是：在不依赖闭源前沿模型、也不走高成本大规模搜索的前提下，怎样把 Lean 4 形式化定理证明做得更强、更稳，而且避免常见 agentic prover 在局部死胡同里反复打转。作者把问题重新表述为“先生成全局证明蓝图，再并行证明子节点，并根据失败节点回写修正全局策略”。关键不在单步 proof search，而在把整个证明过程提升到图级别的规划与迭代。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身，它不是直接的 pretrain 论文；但对 post-train、tool-using reasoning、formal reasoning 数据构造和可验证训练信号有现实启发。它说明了一点：当任务具有强结构约束时，单一长链 CoT 或递归分解未必是最合适的控制流，显式中间表示——这里是 dependency-graph blueprint——可以显著改善搜索效率、并行性和失败恢复。对做 reasoning model 或 theorem proving 数据合成的人，这类“先规划、后局部求解、再全局修正”的范式比单纯 rollout 更接近可扩展系统设计。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是 blueprint。作者把目标定理转成一个 Lean 文件形式的依赖图，节点是 definitions 或 lemmas，边表示证明依赖。流程分三步。第一步，blueprint generation：给定目标 theorem statement，可选地再给一个自然语言证明，模型一次性产出一组形式化子命题及其依赖关系。这里和 Draft-Sketch-Prove 的区别是，后者更像线性 sketch 加 placeholder，而这里是显式图结构，后续可以整体重写。第二步，node proving：对图中开放 lemma 节点，调用带 Lean 编译器和检索工具的 prover，利用其声明依赖并行尝试闭合各节点。并行是关键，因为不同子引理可以共享上游上下文，但不必串行等待。第三步，global refinement：如果某些节点失败，不是继续在局部递归细分，而是把失败信息反馈给 architect，重写整个蓝图，包括替换中间引理、调整依赖、增删定义。作者强调这比 top-down recursion tree 更不容易卡在错误分解上，因为失败会触发全局策略更新，而不是在错误子树里越钻越深。

系统上，它是一个多组件 pipeline：architect 负责图级规划与修订，prover 负责 Lean 证明，检索模块提供 Mathlib 相关上下文。可选的 natural-language proof seed 也值得注意：它不是直接把 informal proof 翻译成 formal sketch，而是把自然语言证明吸收到图结构中，变成命名子引理和依赖关系。这种设计更适合后续 refinement，因为图比平面草稿更容易局部替换和全局重组。

从方法取舍看，作者明确放弃了两条常见路线：一是 one-shot formal proof generation，能力上限受限；二是单 agent 交替调用 Lean 的局部搜索，容易受当前轨迹束缚。Goedel-Architect 选择把“搜索空间控制”前移到 blueprint 层，这更像 program synthesis 里的 high-level plan + subroutine discharge。
summary.experiments:
文中最醒目的结果不是绝对分数，而是性能/成本比。作者声称在其算力档位上建立了新的 Pareto 前沿：使用 open-weight DeepSeek-V4-Flash（文中给出为 284B-A13B）作为骨干，单题成本约 0.44 美元，而表中下一个最强开源 pipeline 约 244 美元/题，成本差了三个数量级左右。摘要和引言给出的对比背景是：公开权重的一次性 prover 在 Putnam 级问题上通常仍停留在个位数到低十几的通过率；超过 50% 的系统大多依赖闭源模型、闭源 pipeline，或极高 API 成本。Goedel-Architect 的卖点是，在开放骨干 + 开放 pipeline 条件下，把性能推到接近这些更昂贵系统的区间。

从全文可提炼的实验关注点有三类。第一，benchmark 主结果：应重点看 MiniF2F、PutnamBench 以及可能的 Putnam 2025 子集结果，尤其是与 open one-shot prover、open agentic pipeline、closed frontier pipeline 的分层对比。第二，ablation：blueprint refinement 是否显著优于不做 refinement、只做局部递归分解、或直接 one-shot sketch；natural-language proof seed 是否在难题上提高初始 blueprint 质量；并行 node proving 对总 wall-clock 和成功率的影响。第三，成本分析：每题 token 用量、architect/prover 调用次数、失败重试开销。对系统论文，这部分往往比单一 pass@1 更说明问题。

当前给出的全文片段没有完整表格数字，因此不宜编造具体通过率；但可以确定的是，作者把“开放性、成本、性能”三者一起作为主结果，而不是只报 solve rate。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先看 Introduction 里对现有 formal prover 的三类划分：one-shot、agentic、pipeline。这里把比较对象和方法定位讲得比较清楚。然后直接看 Figure 1 和 Goedel-Architect 主流程，理解 blueprint 作为全局中间表示到底承载了什么信息。接着看 blueprint generation 与 refinement 的 prompt / schema 设计，重点留意：节点命名、依赖声明、失败反馈如何组织给 architect。再看实验部分的 ablation，判断性能提升究竟来自更强 backbone，还是来自 blueprint 机制本身。

如果只打算花 20-30 分钟，建议顺序是：Introduction → Figure 1 → 主结果表 → blueprint refinement 消融 → 成本表。若要深挖，重点问题有三个：一，失败节点如何被总结成可用于全局重写的信号；二，依赖图是否会引入过度规划，导致简单题反而变慢；三，blueprint 质量是否可以作为可监督中间数据，用于后续训练 architect 或 prover。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles a practical bottleneck in Lean 4 theorem proving: how to get strong formal proving performance without relying on closed frontier models or extremely expensive search-heavy pipelines. The key reframing is to treat proving as iterative global planning over a dependency graph, rather than as one-shot proof generation or purely local recursive decomposition. The system first proposes a proof blueprint, then proves subgoals in parallel, and finally rewrites the global plan when some nodes fail.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it is relevant to post-training, tool-augmented reasoning, and verifiable supervision. The main lesson is structural: for tasks with hard symbolic constraints, explicit intermediate representations can be more effective than long free-form reasoning traces. The blueprint acts as a controllable latent plan. That has implications for theorem-proving data generation, reasoning model training, and any setting where failure signals can be fed back into a higher-level planner instead of only refining the current local trajectory.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The central object is a blueprint: a dependency graph whose nodes are formal definitions and lemmas, and whose edges encode proof dependencies leading to the target theorem. The pipeline has three stages. First, blueprint generation: given the target theorem statement, optionally with a natural-language proof, the architect model emits a Lean file containing formally stated intermediate nodes and declared dependencies. Second, node proving: a tool-using Lean prover attempts to close open lemma nodes, using the declared dependencies and retrieval over Mathlib. These node-level proof attempts can run in parallel, which is important because the graph exposes independent subproblems. Third, global refinement: failed nodes are not handled only by deeper local decomposition. Instead, failure information is sent back to the architect, which can rewrite the blueprint globally by changing intermediate lemmas, adding or removing definitions, or restructuring dependencies.

This differs from recursive decomposition pipelines, where an early bad split can trap the system in an unproductive subtree. It also differs from Draft-Sketch-Prove style approaches. There, the informal proof becomes a flat sketch with placeholders. Here, the optional natural-language proof is converted into a graph of named sublemmas, which is easier to revise and recombine. In system terms, the paper separates high-level strategy formation from low-level proof discharge, and uses the graph as the interface between them.
summary_en.experiments:
The most notable result is the performance-cost tradeoff rather than a single benchmark number. The paper claims a new Pareto point for its compute class using the open-weight DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone, with roughly $0.44 per problem, versus about $244 per problem for the next-best open pipeline reported in the comparison table. The introduction also positions the method against the broader landscape: open one-shot provers remain weak on Putnam-class problems, while systems above the 50% range typically depend on closed models, closed pipelines, or very high API spend.

The experiments to pay attention to are likely in three groups. First, benchmark results on MiniF2F, PutnamBench, and possibly newer Putnam-style sets, with separate comparisons against open one-shot provers, open agentic systems, and closed frontier pipelines. Second, ablations on the blueprint mechanism: whether global refinement helps over no refinement, whether graph-based planning beats recursive decomposition, and whether natural-language proof seeds improve difficult problems. Third, cost accounting: number of architect/prover calls, token usage, and retry overhead. For a systems paper like this, those details matter as much as pass rate.

The provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete result tables, so precise solve-rate numbers should not be inferred beyond what the paper explicitly states in the introduction.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the introduction, especially the taxonomy of prior systems into one-shot provers, agentic provers, and multi-stage pipelines. That framing makes the paper's design choice easier to evaluate. Then read Figure 1 and the main Goedel-Architect section to understand what information the blueprint actually contains and how it is revised. After that, go to the ablations: the key question is whether the gain comes from the blueprint mechanism itself or mostly from the backbone model.

For a 20-30 minute skim, read in this order: introduction, Figure 1, main result table, refinement ablations, and cost table. If reading more carefully, focus on three issues: how failure signals are summarized for global rewriting, whether graph planning adds overhead on easy problems, and whether blueprint traces could become supervised data for training future architect or prover models.

recommendation.zh: 在Lean定理证明上跑出惊人数字，核心是『先全局蓝图再并行填』替代『递归分解』，对推理agent的规划策略有启发。
recommendation.en: Impressive numbers on Lean theorem proving; the core insight — global blueprint first, parallel filling next — is a useful contrast to recursive decomposition for reasoning agents.

paper.title: Skill-RM: Unifying Heterogeneous Evaluation Criteria via Agent Skill
paper.abstract: Reward models (RMs) provide critical feedback signals for LLM post-training, notably in reinforced fine-tuning (RFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines. However, current reward evaluation relies on heterogeneous criteria such as rule-based verifiers, ground-truth references, procedural checklists, and complex rubrics, where a unified mechanism to integrate all types of evidence remains unexplored. To this end, we propose Skill Reward Model (Skill-RM), a unified framework that reformulates

summary.core_problem: 当前 reward model 需整合多种异构评测依据（规则验证器、参考答案、流程 checklist、复杂 rubric 等），但现有 RM 设计要么将复杂证据压缩为不可解释的标量分数，要么依赖非结构化 flat-prompting 把所有资源拼接进一个 prompt，缺乏统一的可复用抽象来编排、选择和聚合异构证据。
summary.importance: 将 reward modeling 重新表述为一个可执行的 agent skill，从被动吸收评测知识变为主动编排资源选择与执行。为 RL/RFT 的 reward 质量提供了一条更可解释且可扩展的路径。
summary.technical_approach: Skill-RM 的核心是把 reward modeling 重新定义为执行一个可复用的『Reward-Evaluation Skill』。这个 skill 遵循 agent skill 中定义的自包含文件系统包：包含 SKILL.md 主文档（编码评测流程）、辅助脚本与资源、元数据。评测时系统执行一个结构化工作流：识别适用标准、选择性调用资源、聚合标准级证据 → 最终 reward。相比 LLM-as-Judge 中的 flat-prompting（仅添加上下文）或原子工具调用（暴露独立可执行文件），skill 封装了编排逻辑——决定何时调用什么资源、如何综合输出如何综合结果。
summary.experiments: 在主流 benchmark 上进行了 best-of-N 重排序和 RFT 实验，Skill-RM 一致优于传统 judge baseline。消融实验确认收益来自 skill 介导的证据编排，而非单纯增加上下文或工具可用性。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读。重点看 Introduction 中对现有 RM 痛点的分析和 Figure 1 的框架图。预计阅读时间约 15 分钟。
summary.authors_note: 机构作者信息未在文中明确标注。

summary_en.core_problem: Reward models must integrate heterogeneous evaluation criteria (rule-based verifiers, ground-truth references, procedural checklists, complex rubrics, etc.). Existing RM designs either compress evidence into uninterpretable scalar scores or rely on unstructured flat-prompting that concatenates all resources into a single prompt, lacking a unified, reusable abstraction for orchestrating, selecting, and aggregating heterogeneous evidence.
summary_en.importance: Reformulates reward modeling as the execution of an executable agent skill, shifting from passive absorption of evaluation knowledge to active orchestration of resource selection and execution. Provides a more interpretable and scalable path for improving reward quality in RL/RFT.
summary_en.technical_approach: Skill-RM redefines reward modeling as executing a reusable 'Reward-Evaluation Skill'. The skill follows the agent-skill abstraction: a self-contained filesystem package containing a main SKILL.md document (encoding the evaluation procedure), auxiliary scripts and resources, and metadata. At evaluation time, the system executes a structured workflow: identify applicable criteria, selectively invoke relevant resources, aggregate criterion-level evidence into a final reward. Unlike flat-prompting (merely adding context) or atomic tool-use (exposing isolated executables), a skill encapsulates orchestration logic—determining what resources to consult, when to invoke them, and how to synthesize outputs.
summary_en.experiments: Extensive experiments on major benchmarks including best-of-N re-ranking and RFT show Skill-RM consistently outperforms traditional judge baselines. Ablation studies confirm gains stem from skill-mediated evidence orchestration rather than merely increased context or tool availability.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim. Focus on the analysis of RM pain points in the Introduction and the framework diagram in Figure 1. Estimated reading time ~15 min.
summary_en.authors_note: Institutional affiliation not explicitly stated in the paper.

recommendation.zh: 将奖励建模转化为智能体任务的思路很有启发性，关注§4的动态证据聚合机制，可用于预训练后期的对齐信号优化。
recommendation.en: The idea of framing reward modeling as an agent task is insightful; focus on Section 4's dynamic evidence aggregation mechanism for alignment signal optimization in late pretraining.

paper.title: On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training
paper.abstract: Tool-calling is a central component of modern large language model (LLM) agents, equipping them with skills beyond their parametric knowledge. This paper studies tool-calling along two complementary axes: effectiveness, i.e., how this capability is measured, and efficiency, i.e., how it is learned. On effectiveness, we systematically analyze tool-calling evaluation pipelines and show that results can be highly sensitive to seemingly minor, often undocumented implementation choices including the

summary.core_problem: 两个核心问题：一是Agent工具调用的评测结果高度依赖未标准化的实现细节，导致结果不可复现、排名不可靠；二是基于RL的工具调用训练存在严重的计算效率瓶颈，包括大量零方差prompt产生无效梯度、策略更新阶段耗时远高于轨迹生成阶段。
summary.importance: 对预训练/后训练闭环研究有两方面具体影响：第一，指出了当前工具调用能力评测的系统性漏洞，为基座工具调用能力的标准化评估提供了校验基准；第二，提出的两个RL训练加速方法可直接推广到通用RLHF/GRPO训练流程，评测部分修正了领域普遍存在的评估偏差，效率部分可带来3-5倍的端到端训练墙钟时间加速，且不损失最终性能，属于RL后训练范式的实用级效率优化。
summary.technical_approach: 研究分为两部分：第一是评测有效性分析，以BFCL基准为案例，控制变量分析随机种子、系统提示词、多轮模板构造、交互历史处理方式等变量对最终性能的影响；第二是训练效率优化，提出两个互补的加速方法：1）在线预轨迹过滤，跳过前k个epoch中轨迹全部正确的prompt，避免冗余采样；2）方差感知的轨迹下采样，仅选择奖励方差最大的子集轨迹用于策略更新，在保留梯度信息量的前提下减少更新阶段的计算量。与现有方法的区别：预过滤方法之前仅在数学推理RL训练中尝试，在工具调用场景下仅需跳过1-2个epoch的正确prompt即可生效；方差感知下采样的现有研究没有专门针对工具调用RL中更新阶段占比极高的特性做适配。
summary.experiments: 评测部分测试了Qwen3-4B、Qwen3-8B、Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct、Llama3.1-8B-Instruct、Llama3.2-3B-Instruct共5个主流模型，发现不同实现细节下的性能波动最高可达20%以上，多轮场景下波动幅度远高于单轮，甚至会导致模型排名反转。训练效率部分训练了Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct（单轮）和Qwen3-4B（多轮）两个模型，发现RL训练中最高80%的prompt属于零方差prompt，即所有轨迹奖励相同、无梯度贡献，策略更新阶段的计算成本是轨迹生成阶段的3-5倍；两个加速方法结合可带来3-5倍的端到端墙钟时间加速，最终工具调用性能与全量训练无统计差异，消融实验显示仅预过滤即可带来约2倍加速，仅方差感知下采样即可带来约1.5-2倍加速。
summary.reading_guide: 精读重点关注第3节的评测变量控制实验，特别是图2-4的性能波动和排名反转结果、第4节的RL训练效率瓶颈分析，即图5-6的零方差比例和时间占比统计、第5节的两个加速方法的消融实验；核心创新点一是对工具调用评测脆弱性的系统性量化，二是针对RL训练中零梯度和更新高成本问题的极简有效优化；值得深挖的点包括：评测脆弱性的结论是否可以推广到其他Agent能力评测、零方差prompt的分布特性是否可以用于训练数据的预处理、方差感知下采样的最优比例是否和任务类型相关。
summary.authors_note: Amazon，作者为Amazon Nova团队研究人员，该团队开发了Nova-1模型，是本次评估的模型之一。

summary_en.core_problem: Two core problems are addressed: first, agent tool-calling evaluation results are highly sensitive to unstandardized implementation details, leading to non-reproducible results and unreliable leaderboard rankings; second, RL-based tool-calling training suffers from severe computational efficiency bottlenecks, including a large share of zero-variance prompts that produce no valid gradients, and policy update stages that take far more time than rollout generation.
summary_en.importance: It delivers two concrete impacts on pretrain-posttrain closed-loop research: first, it identifies systematic flaws in current tool-calling capability evaluation, providing a validation baseline for standardized assessment of foundation model tool-calling capabilities; second, the two proposed RL training acceleration methods can be directly generalized to general RLHF/GRPO training pipelines. The evaluation analysis corrects widespread assessment biases in the field, and the efficiency optimizations deliver 3-5x end-to-end wall-clock speedup without sacrificing final performance, representing a practical efficiency improvement for RL post-training paradigms.
summary_en.technical_approach: Research is split into two parts. For evaluation effectiveness, controlled variable analysis is conducted on the BFCL benchmark to measure the impact of random seeds, system prompts, multi-turn template construction, and interaction history handling on final performance. For training efficiency, two complementary acceleration methods are proposed: 1) Online pre-rollout filtering, which skips prompts whose rollouts were all correct in the previous k epochs to avoid redundant sampling; 2) Variance-aware rollout down-sampling, which selects only the subset of rollouts with the highest reward variance for policy update, reducing update-stage computation while retaining gradient information. Differences from prior work: Pre-filtering was previously only tested on math reasoning RL training. For tool-calling scenarios, skipping correct prompts for just 1-2 epochs is sufficient to deliver gains. Variance-aware down-sampling was not previously adapted to the unique characteristic of tool-calling RL where the update stage dominates wall-clock time.
summary_en.experiments: For evaluation analysis, 5 mainstream models are tested: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct. Performance fluctuations can exceed 20% across different implementation choices, with far larger fluctuations in multi-turn settings than single-turn, even leading to reversed model rankings. For training efficiency, two models are trained: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct for single-turn tool-calling and Qwen3-4B for multi-turn tool-calling. Up to 80% of prompts in RL training are zero-variance prompts with identical rewards across all rollouts and no gradient contribution, and the policy update stage costs 3-5x more computation than rollout generation. The combination of the two acceleration methods delivers 3-5x end-to-end wall-clock speedup with no statistically significant difference in final tool-calling performance compared to full training. Ablation studies show pre-filtering alone delivers ~2x speedup, and variance-aware down-sampling alone delivers ~1.5-2x speedup.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 3 for controlled evaluation variable experiments, especially Figures 2-4 for performance fluctuation and ranking reversal, Section 4 for RL training efficiency bottleneck analysis, specifically Figures 5-6 for zero-variance share and time breakdown, and Section 5 for ablation studies of the two acceleration methods. Core innovations include the systematic quantification of tool-calling evaluation fragility, and simple, effective optimizations for zero-gradient and high update cost issues in RL training. Worth further exploration: whether evaluation fragility findings generalize to other agent capability evaluations, distribution characteristics of zero-variance prompts for training data preprocessing, and whether optimal down-sampling ratio correlates with task type.
summary_en.authors_note: Amazon, authors are researchers from the Amazon Nova team, which developed Nova-1, one of the evaluated models.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会直接改你做 tool-use/RL 的实验习惯：先别信 leaderboard，先复查 prompt、history carry-over 和无效 rollout 比例；至少把评测协议和 token waste 统计补上。
recommendation.en: This should change how you run tool-use/RL experiments: trust no leaderboard before auditing prompt templates, history carry-over, and wasted-rollout ratios; at minimum, add protocol controls and token-waste accounting.

paper.title: CA-BED: Conversation-Aware Bayesian Experimental Design
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at static reasoning tasks, yet their performance often degrades in interactive scenarios where information must be actively acquired through questioning. A key challenge lies in selecting questions that reduce uncertainty while incorporating responses that may be ambiguous or only partially informative. To address this, we propose Conversation-Aware Bayesian Experimental Design (CA-BED), an inference-time probabilistic dialog planning framework that integrates

summary.core_problem: LLM在需要通过提问主动获取信息的交互式场景中表现不佳，关键挑战是如何选择能减少不确定性的问题，同时能处理模糊或部分信息性的回答。
summary.importance: Agent方法创新——提出将贝叶斯实验设计与LLM似然估计结合的概率对话规划框架，在多轮对话中优化问题选择。
summary.technical_approach: CA-BED维护假设上的信念分布，预测可能答案，通过模拟对话树传播期望信息增益；用LLM作为似然估计器处理模糊回答，在推理时规划多轮最优问题序列。
summary.experiments: 在两个结构化实体推理benchmark上，成功率比直接提示平均提升21.8%，与其他信息寻求方法相比有可比增益。
summary.authors_note: 作者含Kevin Zhu等，机构不明确但涉及多所高校。

summary_en.core_problem: LLMs underperform in interactive scenarios requiring active information acquisition through questioning; the challenge is selecting uncertainty-reducing questions while handling ambiguous or partially informative responses.
summary_en.importance: Agent method innovation — proposes a probabilistic dialog planning framework integrating Bayesian Experimental Design with LLM-based likelihood estimation for optimal question selection across multiple conversational turns.
summary_en.technical_approach: CA-BED maintains a belief distribution over hypotheses, anticipates possible answers, propagates expected information gain through a simulated conversation tree; uses LLM as likelihood estimator for ambiguous answers, planning multi-round optimal question sequences at inference time.
summary_en.experiments: Achieves average 21.8% improvement in success rates over direct prompting on two structured entity-deduction benchmarks, with comparable gains relative to alternative information-seeking methods.
summary_en.authors_note: Includes Kevin Zhu among authors; institutions not fully specified but span multiple universities.

recommendation.zh: Agent规划方法有一定技术新意但整体与预训练无关，仅对Agent研究方向有参考价值，扫读方法部分即可。
recommendation.en: Agent planning with some technical novelty but unrelated to pretraining; only relevant to agent research direction; skim the method.

paper.title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks
paper.abstract: LLM agents increasingly face long-horizon tasks such as web search and deep research in real-world applications, where accumulated context can cause long-context degradation and reasoning failures. Prior work mitigates this through context management with agent-side context control or fixed strategies such as summarization, which require training the agent itself for adaptation - making it impractical for closed-source agents and ignoring that different agents may require different strategies. W

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决长程 Agent 中的上下文管理问题：轨迹、工具结果和中间推理不断累积后，长上下文退化会导致约束遗忘、过早放弃和重复探索。传统做法多让 Agent 自己总结或调用上下文工具，但这要求 Agent 具备相应协议能力，也不适合闭源模型。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的启发在于，它把“长上下文可用性”从窗口长度问题转成了 Agent 兼容的上下文分布问题。同样的原始轨迹，对不同能力模型未必都是有益输入；弱模型可能需要更强压缩来降低推理负担，强模型则能保留更多原始证据以维持 fidelity。这个观察对长上下文预训练和 Agent 后训练都有意义：训练目标不能只奖励装入更多 token，还要奖励模型在被裁剪、压缩、重排后的上下文上稳定执行。
summary.technical_approach: AdaCoM 使用一个外部 context manager 管理上下文，任务 Agent 保持冻结。基础流程是 ReAct Agent 在第 t 轮基于 managed context 生成动作，环境返回 observation 后，manager 接收当前上下文并输出结构化修改动作，得到下一轮 managed context。方法有两个关键设计。第一是架构解耦：manager 可以是较小 LLM，不需要训练或修改闭源 Agent。第二是操作灵活：不预设只做摘要，而是允许 manager 对上下文任意部分进行编辑、保留、压缩或重组。manager 通过端到端强化学习训练，奖励来自最终任务表现，因此学到的是某个冻结 Agent 真正能用好的上下文形态，而不是人工规定的摘要格式。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 web search 和 deep research 类型长程任务，并在多种 Agent 上测试。论文报告 AdaCoM 能明显改善任务表现，主要通过减少约束遗忘、过早放弃和冗余探索来取得收益。分析部分提出 Fidelity–Reliability Trade-off：以 vanilla ReAct 表现衡量 Agent 能力时，强 Agent 的 manager 倾向保留更多原始轨迹以减少信息损失；弱 Agent 的 manager 更倾向激进压缩，以降低长上下文干扰并提高执行可靠性。迁移实验显示，训练好的 manager 更容易在能力相近的 Agent 之间迁移，而跨能力层级迁移效果较弱。给定内容未提供具体提升数字，精读时需要回到主实验表格核对各 benchmark 和各 Agent 的增益幅度。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 20–30 分钟。重点看 AdaCoM 方法部分，特别是 managed context 的递推定义、manager 的结构化修改动作空间和强化学习训练流程。实验部分优先看三个信息：不同 Agent 上 AdaCoM 相对 vanilla ReAct 和固定摘要策略的提升；manager 学到的上下文长度和压缩比例；跨 Agent 迁移矩阵。最值得带走的是 Fidelity–Reliability Trade-off，因为它解释了为什么单一摘要策略很难适配所有模型，也解释了为什么长上下文能力评估应同时看信息保真和推理稳定性。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses context management for long-horizon LLM agents. As actions, observations, tool outputs, and intermediate reasoning accumulate, the growing context can hurt later decisions. Existing approaches often ask the agent itself to summarize or manage context, which is fragile for frozen or closed-source agents and assumes a single management strategy works across models.
summary_en.importance: The useful insight is that long-context performance is not only about context-window size. It is also about whether the presented context distribution is compatible with a particular agent. Stronger agents can often use more raw trajectory evidence, while weaker agents may need more aggressive compression to avoid distraction and instruction drift. This has implications for long-context pretraining and agent post-training: models should be trained not just to accept many tokens, but to operate reliably under edited, compressed, and reorganized contexts.
summary_en.technical_approach: AdaCoM introduces an external context manager while keeping the task agent frozen. In a ReAct-style workflow, the agent acts on a managed context; after the environment returns an observation, the manager receives the updated context and emits a structured modification action; applying this action produces the next managed context. The design has two important choices. First, context management is architecturally decoupled from the task agent, so it can be used with closed-source or otherwise untrainable agents. Second, the manager is not restricted to a fixed summarization operation. It can flexibly edit, retain, compress, or reorganize different parts of the trajectory. The manager is trained with end-to-end reinforcement learning using task success signals, so the learned policy is optimized for what the frozen agent can actually use.
summary_en.experiments: The evaluation covers long-horizon web search and deep research tasks across multiple agents. AdaCoM is reported to improve performance by reducing constraint forgetting, premature abandonment, and redundant exploration. The analysis identifies a Fidelity–Reliability trade-off: managers paired with stronger agents preserve more raw trajectory content to maintain evidence fidelity, while managers paired with weaker agents compress more aggressively to keep reasoning reliable. Transfer experiments show that a trained manager transfers best between agents of similar capability, and less reliably across different capability tiers. The provided text does not include exact performance numbers, so the main tables should be checked for benchmark-level gains and ablations.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. Focus on the AdaCoM workflow, the managed-context recurrence, the action space for structured context modification, and the reinforcement learning setup. In the experiments, prioritize comparisons against vanilla ReAct and fixed summarization, the learned context-length or compression behavior, and the transfer matrix across agents. The most relevant part for foundation-model researchers is the Fidelity–Reliability trade-off, because it connects long-context degradation to model capability and suggests why a single context-management heuristic is unlikely to fit all agents.

recommendation.zh: 重点看第5节的Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off实验结论，对长上下文Agent的后训练与策略设计有实际参考价值
recommendation.en: Focus on the Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off results in Section 5, which has practical reference value for post-training and strategy design of long-context agents
